In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the L2 gender processing is a complex phenomenon that involves a number of cognitive mechanisms, and that it is influenced by several factors.
L2 speakers are not able to process grammatical gender at the lexical level, and that this insensitivity is not due to an inability to assign gender to words.
L2 learners do not seem to be sensitive to gender violations at the lexical level.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
L1 and L2 speakers differ in their use of grammatical gender information in the processing of L2 words.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the ability to use grammatical knowledge during L2 processing is not a straightforward matter and that the apparent insensitivity to grammatical violations is likely due to processing constraints rather than a lack of knowledge.
the ability to use grammatical gender information in L2 lexical processing is not a simple function of proficiency, but instead is constrained by the nature of the L2 input.
the ability to use grammatical knowledge during lexical processing is not necessarily an automatic consequence of L2 learning.
